subject: Qualification recap — procurement readiness & security dependencies
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Recap: procurement checklist & security gating items
Attachments: RDW_SOC2_Report_v2024.pdf (pdf), DPA_Template_Redline.docx (docx)

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement has a single checklist to act on. Please feel free to flag anything I missed.

Call notes (short):
- Use case: internal developer platform for doc ingestion/search and clinical summarization pilots.
- Initial scope: 3 teams, ~10 seats, low peak concurrency for Q3 proof-of-concept.
- Priority: data controls and auditability (must pass internal security review).

Procurement/commercial options we discussed (please confirm preferred path):
- Card: fastest (immediate, self-serve) — good for POC but not typical for enterprise purchasing.
- PO / invoice (preferred by many enterprise buyers): Redwood supports net-30 invoices with signed SOW / PO.
- Marketplace (AWS/GCP): available for customers who want consolidated cloud billing; adds a bit of lead time for onboarding.

Security & compliance gating items (what procurement will request):
1) SOC 2 report (Type II preferred) — attached: RDW_SOC2_Report_v2024.pdf (summary).
2) Data Processing Addendum (DPA) — attached redline template for your legal to preview.
3) Completed security questionnaire (SSQ) / third-party risk form — we can fill your standard questionnaire; if you can share the doc we’ll prioritize.
4) Audit log sample / retention policy notes — available on request; can demo in Console.

Asks & next steps:
- Emily / Procurement: confirm preferred billing route (card / PO / marketplace) and timing target for PO issuance.
- Procurement: please share your PO template + any SSQ or procurement forms (I saw you have Atlas_PO_Template.pdf in the procurement repo — attaching what you mentioned would be helpful).
- Redwood (Connor): I’ll share SOC2 summary + points of contact for security/engineering; Marissa will own the DPA redline.

Target timeline: if PO route, target signed PO within 2–3 weeks from confirmation so we can start onboarding in late May.

If helpful I can pull Karthik into the thread for commercial terms (pricing/commit / marketplace cadence).

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Connor O'Brien
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

Thanks, Connor — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Billing path: Procurement will likely require a PO and standard invoicing (net-30). Marketplace is not our preferred route right now because our finance team prefers direct vendor relationships.

2) Security gating: procurement and InfoSec will need
   - SOC 2 Type II (scope that includes hosting and data handling)
   - Completed security questionnaire (I’ll attach the standard vendor SSQ in a follow-up)
   - Confirmation that Redwood’s DPA can be negotiated to our standard terms (we’ll start with the attached PO template and DPA requests)

3) Timeline: Our internal procurement lead (Ravi) is booking a vendor packet review this Thursday. If Redwood can send the SOC2 report and a redlineable DPA by end of Tuesday, that would keep us on schedule.

Ravi — looping you in to coordinate PO template and timing.

Emily

Hi Connor / Emily —

This is Ravi from Atlas procurement. Quick vendor packet questions so we can route internally:

- Payment terms: we need confirmation you accept PO followed by net-30 invoice. Please confirm account details for invoicing and whether you support line-item billing.
- SOC 2 scope: does your SOC2 cover handling of customer PII and hosting in public cloud? We need the report and a description of scope (what systems were in scope).
- Audit logs: can you provide a short write-up describing audit log retention and export? Our security team will want a short demo or a recording.
- DPA redlines: we have a set of mandatory clauses for data residency and subprocessors — please confirm if Redwood can accept or counter.

Please send responses and any artifacts (SOC2, DPA redline, demo link) before Thursday’s vendor packet review, otherwise we’ll have to push to next week.

Thanks,
Ravi Singh
Senior Procurement Manager | Atlas Health
procure@atlashealth.com

Subject: Re: Recap: procurement checklist & security gating items — commercial note

Connor / Marissa — quick note from commercial:

- Billing: We support PO + net-30 for enterprise customers. Onboarding finance will set up an invoice schedule and account code. If Atlas needs line-item billing, we can accommodate but it may add a short reconciliation step.
- Marketplace: Enabled, but as Emily noted, it’s slower for customers who prefer direct vendor management.
- Pricing: For the POC (estimated 3 teams, 10 seats), propose a time-limited eval credit plus invoiced monthly consumption. If Atlas wants committed spend for discounted rates we can discuss a short term reserved capacity commit.
- Legal / DPA: Marissa will handle the DPA redline. For SOC2 scope questions: SOC2 covers infrastructure, change management and logical access controls — it does not include customer-specific data processing tests (we still provide detailed descriptions). We can share a SOC2 cover letter that spells out the scope.

Suggested owner matrix (for the thread):
- Redwood: Connor — overall coordination & demo scheduling.
- Redwood: Marissa — DPA & legal redlines.
- Atlas: Ravi — procurement and PO issuance.
- Atlas: Emily — technical/security contact.

HubSpot link for the deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/RDW-4927

Karthik

All — thanks for the quick responses. Consolidating next steps so Thursday’s vendor packet review has everything it needs:  

Action items (owners & target dates):
1) SOC2 package (Connor): send full SOC2 cover letter + the summary (attached) by EOD Wed (done). If procurement needs the full report we’ll move to an NDA exchange — please confirm.
2) DPA (Marissa): initial redline returned to Atlas legal by EOD Wed; Marissa will include notes on subprocessors and data residency.
3) Security questionnaire (Atlas): Emily / Ravi to send the SSQ to connor@redwood.com by EOD Tue; Redwood will aim to return it within 48 hours.
4) PO template acceptance (Ravi): Procurement to confirm whether your standard PO template is acceptable or requires minor changes; Connor to provide billing account details upon PO confirmation.
5) Demo / audit logs (Connor): schedule a 30-min demo for Atlas security on Friday (or record and share).

If we can close the SOC2 + DPA redline this week and Procurement confirms the PO path, we’ll accept a signed PO and invoice net-30 to begin onboarding. If Atlas prefers marketplace instead, Karthik can outline onboarding lead time (usually 2–3 weeks for marketplace procurement).

Please reply in-thread with any blockers. I’ll follow up after the vendor packet review on Thursday.

Cheers —
Connor O'Brien
